14.2: and Jeroboam says to his wife, `Rise, I pray you, and change yourself, and they know not that you are wife of Jeroboam, and you have gone to Shiloh; indeed, there is Ahijah the prophet; he spoke to me of being king over this people;
14.3: and you have taken in your hand ten loaves, and crumbs, and a bottle of honey, and have gone in to him; he does declare to you what becomes of the youth.'
14.4: And the wife of Jeroboam does so, and rises, and goes to Shiloh, and enters the house of Ahijah, and Ahijah is not able to see, for his eyes have stood because of his age.
14.5: And Jehovah said to Ahijah, `Indeed, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to seek a word from you concerning her son, for he is sick; thus and thus you do speak to her, and it comes to pass at her coming in, that she is making herself strange.'
14.6: And it comes to pass, at Ahijah's hearing the sound of her feet as she came in to the opening, that he says, `Come in, wife of Jeroboam, why is this--you are making yourself strange? and I am sent to you with a sharp thing:
14.7: Go, say to Jeroboam, Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, Because that I have made you high out of the midst of the people, and appoint you leader over my people Israel,
14.8: and rend the kingdom from the house of David, and give it to you, --and you have not been as My servant David who kept My commands, and who walked after Me with all his heart, to do only that which is right in My eyes,
14.9: and you do evil above all who have been before you, and go, and make to you other gods and molten images to provoke Me to anger, and Me you have cast behind your back:
14.10: `Therefore, indeed, I am bringing in evil to the house of Jeroboam, and have cut off to Jeroboam those sitting on the wall--shut up and left--in Israel, and have put away the posterity of the house of Jeroboam, as one puts away the dung till its consumption;
14.11: him who dies of Jeroboam in a city do the dogs eat, and him who dies in a field do fowl of the heavens eat, for Jehovah has spoken.
14.12: `And you, rise, go to your house; in the going in of your feet to the city--has the lad died;
14.13: and all Israel have mourned for him, and buried him, for this one--by himself--comes of Jeroboam to a grave, because there has been found in him a good thing toward Jehovah, God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
14.14: `And Jehovah has raised up for Him a king over Israel who cuts off the house of Jeroboam this day--and what? --even now!
14.15: And Jehovah has smitten Israel as the reed is moved by the waters, and has plucked Israel from off this good ground that He gave to their fathers, and scattered them beyond the River, because that they made their shrines, provoking Jehovah to anger;
14.16: and He gives up Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned, and that he caused Israel to sin.'
14.17: And the wife of Jeroboam rises, and goes, and comes to Tirzah; she has come in to the threshold of the house, and the youth dies;
14.18: and they bury him, and mourn for him do all Israel, according to the word of Jehovah, that he spoke by the hand of His servant Ahijah the prophet.
14.19: And the rest of the matters of Jeroboam, how he fought, and how he reigned, indeed, they are written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
14.20: And the days that Jeroboam reigned are twenty and two years, and he lies with his fathers, and reign does Nadab his son in his stead.
14.21: And Rehoboam son of Solomon has reigned in Judah; a son of forty and one years is Rehoboam in his reigning, and seventeen years he has reigned in Jerusalem, the city that Jehovah chose to set His name there, out of all the tribes of Israel, and the name of his mother is Naamah the Ammonitess.
14.22: And Judah does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and they make Him zealous above all that their fathers did by their sins that they have sinned.
14.23: And they build--also they--for themselves high places, and standing-pillars, and shrines, on every high height, and under every green tree;
14.24: and also a whoremonger has been in the land; they have done according to all the abominations of the nations that Jehovah dispossessed from the presence of the sons of Israel.
14.25: And it comes to pass, in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, gone up has Shishak king of Egypt against Jerusalem,
14.26: and he takes the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the house of the king, yes, the whole he has taken; and he takes all the shields of gold that Solomon made.
14.27: And king Rehoboam makes in their stead shields of brass, and has made them a charge on the hand of the heads of the runners, those keeping the opening of the house of the king,
14.28: and it comes to pass, from the going in of the king to the house of Jehovah, the runners bear them, and have brought them back to the chamber of the runners.
14.29: And the rest of the matters of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
14.30: And war has been between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days;
14.31: and Rehoboam lies with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers, in the city of David, and the name of his mother is Naamah the Ammonitess, and reign does Abijam his son in his stead.

15.1: And in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam son of Nebat, reigned has Abijam over Judah;
15.2: three years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Maachah daughter of Abishalom;
15.3: and he walks in all the sins of his father, that he did before him, and his heart has not been perfect with Jehovah his God, as the heart of David his father;
15.4: but for David's sake has Jehovah his God given to him a lamp in Jerusalem, to raise up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem,
15.5: in that David did that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, and turned not aside from all that He commanded him all days of his life--only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite;
15.6: and war has been between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
15.7: And the rest of the matters of Abijam, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah? And war has been between Abijam and Jeroboam;
15.8: and Abijam lies with his fathers, and they bury him in the city of David, and reign does Asa his son in his stead.
15.9: And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned has Asa over Judah,
15.10: and forty and one years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Maachah daughter of Abishalom.
15.11: And Asa does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, like David his father,
15.12: and removes the whoremongers out of the land, and turns aside all the idols that his fathers made;
15.13: and also Maachah his mother--he turns her aside from being mistress, in that she made a horrible thing for a shrine, and Asa cuts down her horrible thing, and burns it by the brook Kidron;
15.14: and the high places have not turned aside; only, the heart of Asa has been perfect with Jehovah all his days,
15.15: and he brings in the sanctified things of his father, and his own sanctified things, to the house of Jehovah, silver, and gold, and vessels.
15.16: And war has been between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days,
15.17: and Baasha king of Israel goes up against Judah, and builds Ramah, not to permit any one going out and coming in to Asa king of Judah.
15.18: And Asa takes all the silver and the gold that are left in the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the house of the king, and gives them into the hand of his servants, and king Asa sends them to Ben-Hadad, son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion king of Aram, who is dwelling in Damascus, saying,
15.19: `A covenant is between me and you, between my father and your father; indeed, I have sent to you a reward of silver and gold; go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, and he goes up from off me.'
15.20: And Ben-Hadad hearkens to king Asa, and sends the heads of the forces that he has against cities of Israel, and smites Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-Beth-Maachah, and all Chinneroth, besides all the land of Naphtali;
15.21: and it comes to pass at Baasha's hearing, that he ceases from building Ramah, and dwells in Tirzah.
15.22: And king Asa has summoned all Judah--there is none exempt--and they lift up the stones of Ramah, and its wood, that Baasha has built, and king Asa builds with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.
15.23: And the rest of all the matters of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities that he built, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah? Only, at the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet;
15.24: and Asa lies with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his stead.
15.25: And Nadab son of Jeroboam has reigned over Israel, in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigns over Israel two years,
15.26: and does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and goes in the way of his father, and in his sin that he made Israel to sin.
15.27: And conspire against him does Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, and Baasha smites him in Gibbethon, which is to the Philistines--and Nadab and all Israel are laying siege against Gibbethon--
15.28: yes, Baasha puts him to death in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigns in his stead.
15.29: And it comes to pass, at his reigning, he has smitten the whole house of Jeroboam, he has not left any breathing to Jeroboam till his destroying him, according to the word of Jehovah, that He spoke by the hand of His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
15.30: because of the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned, and that he caused Israel to sin, by his provocation with which he provoked to anger Jehovah, God of Israel.
15.31: And the rest of the matters of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
15.32: And war has been between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
15.33: In the third year of Asa king of Judah reigned has Baasha son of Ahijah over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years,
15.34: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and walks in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin that he caused Israel to sin.

16.1: And a word of Jehovah is to Jehu son of Hanani, against Baasha, saying,
16.2: `Because that I have raised you up out of the dust, and appoint you leader over My people Israel, and you walk in the way of Jeroboam, and cause My people Israel to sin--to provoke Me to anger with their sins;
16.3: indeed, I am putting away the posterity of Baasha, even the posterity of his house, and have given up your house as the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat;
16.4: him who dies of Baasha in a city do the dogs eat, and him who dies of his in a field do fowl of the heavens eat.'
16.5: And the rest of the matters of Baasha, and that which he did, and his might, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
16.6: And Baasha lies with his fathers, and is buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigns in his stead.
16.7: And also by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani the prophet a word of Jehovah has been concerning Baasha, and concerning his house, and concerning all the evil that he did in the eyes of Jehovah to provoke Him to anger with the work of his hands, to be like the house of Jeroboam, and concerning that for which he smote him.
16.8: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah reigned has Elah son of Baasha over Israel in Tirzah, two years;
16.9: and conspire against him does his servant Zimri (head of the half of the chariots) and he is in Tirzah drinking--a drunkard in the house of Arza, who is over the house in Tirzah.
16.10: And Zimri comes in and smites him, and puts him to death, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigns in his stead;
16.11: and it comes to pass in his reigning, at his sitting on his throne, he has smitten the whole house of Baasha; he has not left to him any sitting on the wall, and of his redeemers, and of his friends.
16.12: And Zimri destroys the whole house of Baasha, according to the word of Jehovah, that He spoke concerning Baasha, by the hand of Jehu the prophet:
16.13: concerning all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, that they sinned, and that they caused Israel to sin to provoke Jehovah, God of Israel, with their vanities.
16.14: And the rest of the matters of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
16.15: In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, reigned has Zimri seven days in Tirzah; and the people are encamping against Gibbethon, which is to the Philistines;
16.16: and the people who are encamping hear, saying, `Zimri has conspired, and also has smitten the king;' and all Israel cause Omri head of the host to reign over Israel on that day in the camp.
16.17: And Omri goes up, and all Israel with him, from Gibbethon, and they lay siege to Tirzah.
16.18: And it comes to pass, at Zimri's seeing that the city has been captured, that he comes in to a high place of the house of the king, and burns over him the house of the king with fire, and dies,
16.19: for his sins that he sinned, to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, to walk in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin that he did, to cause Israel to sin;
16.20: and the rest of the matters of Zimri, and his conspiracy that he made, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
16.21: Then are the sons of Israel parted into halves; half of the people has been after Tibni son of Ginath to cause him to reign, and the half after Omri;
16.22: and stronger are the people that are after Omri than the people that are after Tibni son of Ginath, and Tibni dies, and Omri reigns.
16.23: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah reigned has Omri over Israel twelve years; in Tirzah he has reigned six years,
16.24: and he buys the mount Samaria from Shemer, with two talents of silver, and builds on the mount, and calls the name of the city that he has built by the name of Shemer, lord of the hill--Samaria.
16.25: And Omri does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and does evil above all who are before him,
16.26: and walks in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sin that he caused Israel to sin, to provoke Jehovah, God of Israel, with their vanities.
16.27: And the rest of the matters of Omri that he did, and his might that he got, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
16.28: And Omri lies with his fathers, and is buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigns in his stead.
16.29: And Ahab son of Omri has reigned over Israel in the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab son of Omri reigns over Israel in Samaria twenty and two years,
16.30: and Ahab son of Omri does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah above all who are before him.
16.31: And it comes to pass--has it been light his walking in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat? --then he takes a wife, Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians, and goes and serves Baal, and bows himself to it,
16.32: and raises up an altar for Baal, in the house of the Baal, that he built in Samaria;
16.33: and Ahab makes the shrine, and Ahab adds to do so as to provoke Jehovah, God of Israel, above all the kings of Israel who have been before him.
16.34: In his days has Hiel the Beth-Elite built Jericho; in Abiram his first-born he laid its foundation, and in Segub his youngest he set up its doors, according to the word of Jehovah that He spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.

17.1: And Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, says to Ahab, `Jehovah, God of Israel, lives, before whom I have stood, there is not these years dew and rain, except according to my word.'
17.2: And the word of Jehovah is to him, saying,
17.3: `Go from this place; and you have turned for you eastward, and been hidden by the brook Cherith, that is on the front of the Jordan,
17.4: and it has been, from the brook you do drink, and the ravens I have commanded to sustain you there.'
17.5: And he goes and does according to the word of Jehovah, yes, he goes and dwells by the brook Cherith, that is on the front of the Jordan,
17.6: and the ravens are bringing to him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening, and of the brook he drinks.
17.7: And it comes to pass, at the end of days, that the brook dries up, for there has been no rain in the land,
17.8: and the word of Jehovah is to him, saying,
17.9: `Rise, go to Zarephath, that is to Zidon, and you have dwelt there; indeed, I have commanded there a widow woman to sustain you.'
17.10: And he rises, and goes to Zarephath, and comes in to the opening of the city, and indeed there, a widow woman gathering sticks, and he calls to her, and says, `Bring, I pray you, to me, a little water in a vessel, and I drink.'
17.11: And she goes to bring it, and he calls to her and says, `Bring, I pray you, to me a morsel of bread in your hand.'
17.12: And she says, `Jehovah your God lives, I have not a cake, but the fulness of the hand of meal in a pitcher, and a little oil in a dish; and indeed, I am gathering two sticks, and have gone in and prepared it for myself, and for my son, and we have eaten it--and died.'
17.13: And Elijah says to her, `Fear not, go, do according to your word, only make for me from there a little cake, in the first place, and you have brought out to me; and for you and for your son make--last;
17.14: for thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, The pitcher of meal is not consumed, and the dish of oil is not lacking, till the day of Jehovah's giving a shower on the face of the ground.'
17.15: And she goes, and does according to the word of Elijah, and she eats, she and he, and her household--days;
17.16: the pitcher of meal was not consumed, and the dish of oil did not lack, according to the word of Jehovah that He spoke by the hand of Elijah.
17.17: And it comes to pass, after these things, the son of the woman, mistress of the house, has been sick, and his sickness is very severe till that no breath has been left in him.
17.18: And she says to Elijah, `What--to me and to you, O man of God? you have come to me to cause my iniquity to be remembered, and to put my son to death!'
17.19: And he says to her, `Give to me your son;' and he takes him out of her bosom, and takes him up to the upper chamber where he is abiding, and lays him on his own bed,
17.20: and cries to Jehovah, and says, `Jehovah my God, also on the widow with whom I am sojourning have You done evil--to put her son to death?'
17.21: And he stretches himself out on the lad three times, and calls to Jehovah, and says, `O Jehovah my God, let turn back, I pray You, the soul of this lad into his midst;'
17.22: and Jehovah hearkens to the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the lad turns back into his midst, and he lives.
17.23: And Elijah takes the lad, and brings him down from the upper chamber of the house, and gives him to his mother, and Elijah says, `See, your son lives!'
17.24: And the woman says to Elijah, `Now, this I have known, that a man of God you are, and the word of Jehovah in your mouth is truth.'

18.1: And the days are many, and the word of Jehovah has been to Elijah in the third year, saying, `Go, appear to Ahab, and I give rain on the face of the ground;'
18.2: and Elijah goes to appear to Ahab. And the famine is severe in Samaria,
18.3: and Ahab calls to Obadiah, who is over the house--and Obadiah has been fearing Jehovah greatly,
18.4: and it comes to pass, in Jezebel's cutting off the prophets of Jehovah, that Obadiah takes a hundred prophets, and hides them, fifty men in a cave, and has sustained them with bread and water--
18.5: and Ahab says to Obadiah, `Go through the land, to all fountains of waters, and to all the brooks, if so be we find hay, and keep alive horse and mule, and do not cut off any of the cattle.'
18.6: And they apportion to themselves the land, to pass over into it; Ahab has gone in one way by himself, and Obadiah has gone in another way by himself;
18.7: and Obadiah is in the way, and indeed, Elijah--to meet him; and he discerns him, and falls on his face, and says, `Are you he--my lord Elijah?'
18.8: And he says to him, `I am; go, say to your lord, Indeed, Elijah.'
18.9: And he says, `What have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Ahab--to put me to death?
18.10: Jehovah your God lives, if there is a nation and kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you; and they said, He is not, then he caused the kingdom and the nation to swear, that it does not find you;
18.11: and now, you are saying, Go, say to your lord, Indeed, Elijah;
18.12: and it has been, I go from you, and the Spirit of Jehovah does lift you up, where I know not, and I have come to declare to Ahab, and he does not find you, and he has slain me; and your servant is fearing Jehovah from my youth.
18.13: `Has it not been declared to my lord that which I have done in Jezebel's slaying the prophets of Jehovah, that I hide of the prophets of Jehovah a hundred men, fifty by fifty in a cave, and sustained them with bread and water?
18.14: and now you are saying, Go, say to my lord, Indeed, Elijah--and he has slain me!'
18.15: And Elijah says, `Jehovah of Hosts lives, before whom I have stood, surely to-day I appear to him.'
18.16: And Obadiah goes to meet Ahab, and declares it to him, and Ahab goes to meet Elijah,
18.17: and it comes to pass at Ahab's seeing Elijah, that Ahab says to him, `Are you he--the troubler of Israel?'
18.18: And he says, `I have not troubled Israel, but you and the house of your father, in your forsaking the commands of Jehovah, and you go after the Baalim;
18.19: and now, send, gather to me all Israel, to the mount of Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the shrine, four hundred--eating at the table of Jezebel.'
18.20: And Ahab sends among all the sons of Israel, and gathers the prophets to the mount of Carmel;
18.21: and Elijah comes nigh to all the people, and says, `Till when are you leaping on the two branches? --if Jehovah is God, go after Him; and if Baal, go after him;' and the people have not answered him a word.
18.22: And Elijah says to the people, `I--I have been left a prophet of Jehovah--by myself; and the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men;
18.23: and let them give to us two bullocks, and they choose for themselves the one bullock, and cut it in pieces, and place it on the wood, and place no fire; and I--I prepare the other bullock, and have put it on the wood, and fire I do not place; --
18.24: and you have called in the name of your god, and I--I call in the name of Jehovah, and it has been, the god who answers by fire--He is the God.' And all the people answer and say, `Good is the word.'
18.25: And Elijah says to the prophets of Baal, `Choose for you the one bullock, and prepare first, for you are the multitude, and call you in the name of your god, and place no fire.'
18.26: And they take the bullock that one gave to them, and prepare, and call in the name of Baal from the morning even till the noon, saying, `O Baal, answer us!' and there is no voice, and there is none answering; and they leap on the altar that one had made.
18.27: And it comes to pass, at noon, that Elijah plays on them, and says, `Call with a loud voice, for he is a god, for he is meditating, or pursuing, or on a journey; it may be he is asleep, an does awake.'
18.28: And they call with a loud voice, and cut themselves, according to their ordinance, with swords and with spears, till a flowing of blood is on them;
18.29: and it comes to pass, at the passing by of the noon, that they feign themselves prophets till the going up of the present, and there is no voice, and there is none answering, and there is none attending.
18.30: And Elijah says to all the people, `Come nigh to me;' and all the people come nigh to him, and he repairs the altar of Jehovah that is broken down;
18.31: and Elijah takes twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of Jehovah was, saying, `Israel is your name;'
18.32: and he builds with the stones an altar, in the name of Jehovah, and makes a trench, as about the space of two measures of seed, round about the altar.
18.33: And he arranges the wood, and cuts in pieces the bullock, and places it on the wood, and says, `Fill you four pitchers of water, and pour on the burnt-offering, and on the wood;
18.34: and he says, `Do it a second time;' and they do it a second time; and he says, `Do it a third time;' and they do it a third time;
18.35: and the water goes round about the altar, and also, the trench he has filled with water.
18.36: And it comes to pass, at the going up of the evening- present, that Elijah the prophet comes nigh and says, `Jehovah, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to-day let it be known that You are God in Israel, and I Your servant, that by Your word I have done the whole of these things;
18.37: answer me, O Jehovah, answer me, and this people does know that You are Jehovah God; and You have turned their heart backward.'
18.38: And there falls a fire of Jehovah, and consumes the burnt-offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and the water that is in the trench it has licked up.
18.39: And all the people see, and fall on their faces, and say, `Jehovah, He is the God, Jehovah, He is the God.'
18.40: And Elijah says to them, `Catch you the prophets of Baal; let not a man escape of them;' and they catch them, and Elijah brings them down to the stream Kishon, and does slaughter them there.
18.41: And Elijah says to Ahab, `Go up, eat and drink, because of the sound of the noise of the shower.'
18.42: And Ahab goes up to eat, and to drink, and Elijah has gone up to the top of Carmel, and he stretches himself out on the earth, and he places his face between his knees,
18.43: and says to his young man, `Go up, I pray you, look attentively the way of the sea;' and he goes up and looks attentively, and says, `There is nothing;' and he says, `Turn back,' seven times.
18.44: And it comes to pass, at the seventh, that he says, `Indeed, a little thickness as the palm of a man is coming up out of the sea.' And he says, `Go up, say to Ahab, `Bind--and go down, and the shower does not restrain you.'
18.45: And it comes to pass, in the meantime, that the heavens have become black--thick clouds and wind--and the shower is great; and Ahab rides, and goes to Jezreel,
18.46: and the hand of Jehovah has been on Elijah, and he girds up his loins, and runs before Ahab, till your entering Jezreel.

19.1: And Ahab declares to Jezebel all that Elijah did, and all how he slew all the prophets by the sword,
19.2: and Jezebel sends a messenger to Elijah, saying, `Thus does the gods, and thus do they add, surely about this time to-morrow, I make your life as the life of one of them.'
19.3: And he fears, and rises, and goes for his life, and comes in to Beer-Sheba, that is Judah's, and leaves his young man there,
19.4: and he himself has gone into the wilderness a day's Journey, and comes and sits under a certain retem-tree, and desires his soul to die, and says, `Enough, now, O Jehovah, take my soul, for I am not better than my fathers.'
19.5: And he lies down and sleeps under a certain retem-tree, and indeed, a messenger comes against him, and says to him, `Rise, eat;'
19.6: and he looks attentively, and indeed, at his bolster a cake baken on burning stones, and a dish of water, and he eats, and drinks, and turns, and lies down.
19.7: And the messenger of Jehovah turns back a second time, and comes against him, and says, `Rise, eat, for the way is too great for you;'
19.8: and he rises, and eats, and drinks, and goes in the power of that food forty days and forty nights, to the mount of God--Horeb.
19.9: And he comes in there, to the cave, and lodges there, and indeed, the word of Jehovah is to him, and says to him, `What--to you, here, Elijah?'
19.10: And he says, `I have been very zealous for Jehovah, God of Hosts, for the sons of Israel have forsaken Your covenant--Your altars they have thrown down, and Your prophets they have slain by the sword, and I am left, I, by myself, and they seek my life--to take it.'
19.11: And He says, `Go out, and you have stood in the mount before Jehovah.' And indeed, Jehovah is passing by, and a wind--great and strong--is rending mountains, and shivering rocks before Jehovah: --not in the wind is Jehovah; and after the wind a shaking: --not in the shaking is Jehovah;
19.12: and after the shaking a fire: --not in the fire is Jehovah; and after the fire a voice still small;
19.13: and it comes to pass, at Elijah's hearing it, that he wraps his face in his robe, and goes out, and stands at the opening of the cave, and indeed, to him is a voice, and it says, `What--to you, here, Elijah?'
19.14: And he says, `I have been very zealous for Jehovah, God of Hosts; for the sons of Israel have forsaken Your covenant, Your altars they have thrown down, and Your prophets they have slain by the sword, and I am left, I, by myself, and they seek my life--to take it.'
19.15: And Jehovah says to him, `Go turn back on your way to the wilderness of Damascus, and you have gone in, and anointed Hazael for king over Aram,
19.16: and Jehu son of Nimshi you do anoint for king over Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat, of Abel-Meholah, you do anoint for prophet in your stead.
19.17: `And it has been, him who is escaped from the sword of Hazael, put to death does Jehu, and him who is escaped from the sword of Jehu put to death does Elisha;
19.18: and I have left in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.'
19.19: And he goes from there, and finds Elisha son of Shaphat, and he is plowing; twelve yoke are before him, and he is with the twelfth; and Elijah passes over to him, and casts his robe upon him,
19.20: and he forsakes the oxen, and runs after Elijah, and says, `Let me give a kiss, I pray you, to my father and to my mother, and I go after you.' And he says to him, `Go, turn back, for what have I done to you?'
19.21: And he turns back from after him, and takes the yoke of oxen, and sacrifices it, and with instruments of the oxen he has boiled their flesh, and gives to the people, and they eat, and he rises, and goes after Elijah, and serves him.

20.1: And Ben-Hadad king of Aram has gathered all his force, and thirty and two kings are with him, and horse and chariot, and he goes up and lays siege against Samaria, and fights with it,
20.2: and sends messengers to Ahab king of Israel, to the city,
20.3: and says to him, `Thus said Ben-Hadad, `Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your sons--the best--are mine.'
20.4: And the king of Israel answers and says, `According to your word, my lord, O king: I am yours, and all that I have.'
20.5: And the messengers turn back and say, `Thus spoke Ben-Hadad, saying, Surely I sent to you, saying, Your silver, and your gold, and your wives, and your sons, to me you do give;
20.6: for if, at this time to-morrow, I send my servants to you then they have searched your house, and the houses of your servants, and it has been, every desirable thing of your eyes they place in their hand, and have taken away.'
20.7: And the king of Israel calls to all the elders of the land, and says, `Know, I pray you, and see that evil this one is seeking, for he sent to me for my wives, and for my sons, and for my silver, and for my gold, and I withheld not from him.'
20.8: And all the elders and all the people say to him, `Do not hearken, nor consent.'
20.9: And he says to the messengers of Ben-Hadad, `Say to my lord the king, All that you did send for to your servant at the first I do, and this thing I am not able to do;' and the messengers go and take him back word.
20.10: And Ben-Hadad sends to him, and says, `Thus do the gods to me, and thus do they add, if the dust of Samaria suffice for handfuls for all the people who are at my feet.'
20.11: And the king of Israel answers and says, `Speak you: let not him who is girding on boast himself as him who is loosing his armour.'
20.12: And it comes to pass at the hearing of this word--and he is drinking, he and the kings, in the booths--that he says to his servants, `Set yourselves;' and they set themselves against the city.
20.13: And indeed, a certain prophet has come nigh to Ahab king of Israel, and says, `Thus said Jehovah, `Have you seen all this great multitude? indeed, I am giving it into your hand to-day, and you have known that I am Jehovah.'
20.14: And Ahab says, `By whom?' and he says, `Thus said Jehovah, By the young men of the heads of the provinces;' and he says, `Who does direct the battle?' and he says, `You.'
20.15: And he inspects the young men of the heads of the provinces, and they are two hundred, two and thirty, and after them he has inspects the whole of the people, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand,
20.16: and they go out at noon, and Ben-Hadad is drinking--drunk in the booths, he and the kings, the thirty and two kings, helping him.
20.17: And the young men of the heads of the provinces go out at the first, and Ben-Hadad sends, and they declare to him, saying, `Men have come out of Samaria.'
20.18: And he says, `If for peace they have come out--catch them alive; and if for battle they have come out--alive catch them.'
20.19: And these have gone out of the city--the young men of the heads of the provinces--and the force that is after them,
20.20: and smite each his man, and Aram flees, and Israel pursues them, and Ben-Hadad king of Aram escapes on a horse, and the horsemen;
20.21: and the king of Israel goes out, and smites the horses, and the charioteers, and has smitten among the Aramaeans a great smiting.
20.22: And the prophet comes nigh to the king of Israel, and says to him, `Go, strengthen yourself, and know and see that which you do, for at the turn of the year the king of Aram is coming up against you.'
20.23: And the servants of the king of Aram said to him, `Gods of hills are their gods, therefore they were stronger than we; and yet, we fight with them in the plain--are we not stronger than they?
20.24: `And this thing do you: turn aside the kings each out of his place, and set captains in their stead;
20.25: and you, number to you a force as the force that is fallen from you, and horse for horse, and chariot for chariot, and we fight with them in the plain; are we not stronger than they?' and he hearkens to their voice, and does so.
20.26: And it comes to pass at the turn of the year, that Ben-Hadad inspects the Aramaeans, and goes up to Aphek, to battle with Israel,
20.27: and the sons of Israel have been inspected, and supported, and go to meet them, and the sons of Israel encamp before them, like two flocks of goats, and the Aramaeans have filled the land.
20.28: And there comes nigh a man of God, and speaks to the king of Israel, and says, `Thus said Jehovah, Because that the Aramaeans have said, God of hills is Jehovah, and He is not God of valleys--I have given the whole of this great multitude into your hand, and you have known that I am Jehovah.'
20.29: And they encamp one over-against another seven days, and it comes to pass on the seventh day, that the battle draws near, and the sons of Israel smite Aram--a hundred thousand footmen in one day.
20.30: And those left flee to Aphek, to the city, and the wall falls on twenty and seven chief men who are left, and Ben-Hadad has fled, and comes in to the city, into the innermost part.
20.31: And his servants say to him, `Indeed, we pray you, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel--that they are kind kings; let us put, we pray you, sackcloth on our loins, and ropes on our heads, and we go out to the king of Israel; it may be he does keep you alive.'
20.32: And they gird sackcloth on their loins, and ropes are on their heads, and they come in to the king of Israel, and say, `Your servant Ben-Hadad has said, Let me live, I pray you;' and he says, `Is he yet alive? he is my brother.'
20.33: And the men observe diligently, and hasten, and catch it from him, and say, `Your brother Ben-Hadad;' and he says, `Go you in, bring him;' and Ben-Hadad comes out to him, and he causes him to come up on the chariot.
20.34: And he says to him, `The cities that my father took from your father, I give back, and streets you do make for you in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria;' --`and I, with a covenant, send you away;' and he makes with him a covenant, and sends him away.
20.35: And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his neighbour by the word of Jehovah, `Smite me, I pray you;' and the man refuses to smite him,
20.36: and he says to him, `Because that you have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah, indeed, you are going from me, and the lion has smitten you;' and he goes from him, and the lion finds him, and smites him.
20.37: And he finds another man, and says, `Smite me, I pray you;' and the man smites him, smiting and wounding,
20.38: and the prophet goes and stands for the king on the way, and disguises himself with ashes on his eyes.
20.39: And it comes to pass--the king is passing by--that he has cried to the king, and says, `Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and indeed, a man has turned aside and brings in to me a man, and says, Keep this man; if he be at all missing, then has your life been for his life, or a talent of silver you do weigh out;
20.40: and it comes to pass, your servant is working here and there, and he is not!' and the king of Israel says to him, Right is your judgment; you have determined it.'
20.41: And he hastes and turns aside the ashes from off his eyes, and the king of Israel discerns him, that he is of the prophets,
20.42: and he says to him, `Thus said Jehovah, Because you have sent away the man I devoted, out of your hand, even your life has been for his life, and your people for his people;'
20.43: and the king of Israel goes to his house, sulky and wroth, and comes in to Samaria.

21.1: And it comes to pass, after these things, a vineyard has been to Naboth the Jezreelite, that is in Jezreel, near the palace of Ahab king of Samaria,
21.2: and Ahab speaks to Naboth, saying, `Give to me your vineyard, and it is to me for a garden of green herbs, for it is near by my house, and I give to you in its stead a better vineyard than it; if good in your eyes, I give to you silver--its price.'
21.3: And Naboth says to Ahab, `Far be it from me, by Jehovah, my giving the inheritance of my fathers to you;'
21.4: and Ahab comes in to his house, sulky and wroth, because of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite has spoken to him when he says, `I do not give to you the inheritance of my fathers,' and he lies down on his bed, and turns round his face, and has not eaten bread.
21.5: And Jezebel his wife comes in to him, and speaks to him, `What is this? --your spirit sulky, and you are not eating bread!'
21.6: And he says to her, `Because I speak to Naboth the Jezreelite, and say to him, Give to me your vineyard for money, or if you desire, I give to you a vineyard in its stead; and he says, I do not give to you my vineyard.'
21.7: And Jezebel his wife says to him, `You now do execute rule over Israel! rise, eat bread, and let your heart be glad, --I do give to you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.'
21.8: And she writes letters in the name of Ahab, and seals with his seal, and sends the letters to the elders, and to the freemen, who are in his city, those dwelling with Naboth,
21.9: and she writes in the letters, saying, `Proclaim a fast, and cause Naboth to sit at the head of the people,
21.10: and cause two men--sons of worthlessness--to sit over-against him, and they testify of him, saying, You have blessed God and Melech; and they have brought him out, and stoned him, and he dies.'
21.11: And the men of his city, the elders and the freemen who are dwelling in his city, do as Jezebel has sent to them, as written in the letters that she sent to them,
21.12: they have proclaimed a fast, and caused Naboth to sit at the head of the people,
21.13: and two men--sons of worthlessness--come in, and sit over-against him, and the men of worthlessness testify of him, even Naboth, before the people, saying, `Naboth blessed God and Melech;' and they take him out to the outside of the city, and stone him with stones, and he dies;
21.14: and they send to Jezebel, saying, `Naboth was stoned, and is dead.'
21.15: And it comes to pass, at Jezebel's hearing that Naboth has been stoned, and is dead, that Jezebel says to Ahab, `Rise, possess the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, that he refused to give to you for money, for Naboth is not alive but dead.'
21.16: And it comes to pass, at Ahab's hearing that Naboth is dead, that Ahab rises to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to possess it.
21.17: And the word of Jehovah is to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
21.18: `Rise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria, --indeed, in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to possess it,
21.19: and you have spoken to him, saying, Thus said Jehovah, Have you murdered, and also possessed? and you have spoken to him, saying, Thus said Jehovah, In the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, do the dogs lick your blood, even yours.'
21.20: And Ahab says to Elijah, `Have you found me, O my enemy?' and he says, `I have found--because of your selling yourself to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah;
21.21: indeed, I am bringing in to you evil, and have taken away your posterity, and cut off to Ahab those sitting on the wall, and restrained, and left, in Israel,
21.22: and given up your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, for the provocation with which you have provoked Me, and do cause Israel to sin.
21.23: `And also of Jezebel has Jehovah spoken, saying, The dogs do eat Jezebel in the bulwark of Jezreel;
21.24: him who dies of Ahab in a city do the dogs eat, and him who dies in a field do fowl of the heavens eat;
21.25: surely there has none been like Ahab, who sold himself to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, whom Jezebel his wife has moved,
21.26: and he does very abominably to go after the idols, according to all that the Amorite did whom Jehovah dispossessed from the presence of the sons of Israel.'
21.27: And it comes to pass, at Ahab's hearing these words, that he rends his garments, and puts sackcloth on his flesh, and fasts, and lies in sackcloth, and goes gently.
21.28: And the word of Jehovah is to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
21.29: `Have you seen that Ahab has been humbled before Me? because that he has been humbled before Me, I bring not in the evil in his days; in the days of his son I bring in the evil on his house.'

22.1: And they sit still three years, there is no war between Aram and Israel,
22.2: and it comes to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat king of Judah comes down to the king of Israel,
22.3: and the king of Israel says to his servants, `Have you not known that ours is Ramoth-Gilead? and we are keeping silent from taking it out of the hand of the king of Aram!'
22.4: And he says to Jehoshaphat, `Do you go with me to battle to Ramoth-Gilead?' and Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, `As I am, so you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.'
22.5: And Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, `Seek, I pray you, to-day, the word of Jehovah;'
22.6: and the king of Israel gathers the prophets, about four hundred men, and says to them, `Do I go against Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or do I forbear?' and they say, `Go up, and the Lord does give it into the hand of the king.'
22.7: And Jehoshaphat says, `Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah besides, and we seek by him?'
22.8: And the king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, `Yet--one man to seek Jehovah by him, and I have hated him, for he does not prophesy concerning me good, but evil--Micaiah son of Imlah;' and Jehoshaphat says, `Let not the king say so.'
22.9: And the king of Israel calls to a certain eunuch, and says, `Hasten Micaiah son of Imlah.'
22.10: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah are sitting, each on his throne, clothed with garments, in a threshing-floor, at the opening of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets are prophesying before them.
22.11: And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah makes for himself horns of iron, and says, `Thus said Jehovah, By these you do push the Aramaeans till they are consumed;'
22.12: and all the prophets are prophesying so, saying, `Go up to Ramoth-Gilead, and prosper, and Jehovah has given it into the hand of the king.'
22.13: And the messenger who has gone to call Micaiah has spoken to him, saying, `Indeed, I pray you, the words of the prophets, with one mouth, are good toward the king; let it be, I pray you, your word as the word of one of them--and you have spoken good.'
22.14: And Micaiah says, `Jehovah lives; surely that which Jehovah says to me--it I speak.'
22.15: And he comes in to the king, and the king says to him, `Micaiah, do we go to Ramoth-Gilead, to battle, or do we forbear?' and he says to him, `Go up, and prosper, and Jehovah has given it into the hand of the king.'
22.16: And the king says to him, `How many times am I adjuring you that you speak nothing to me but truth in the name of Jehovah?'
22.17: And he says, `I have seen all Israel scattered on the hills as sheep that have no shepherd, and Jehovah says, These have no master; they turn back each to his house in peace.'
22.18: And the king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, `Have I not said to you, He does not prophesy of me good, but evil?'
22.19: And he says, `Therefore, hear a word of Jehovah; I have seen Jehovah sitting on His throne, and all the host of the heavens standing by Him, on His right and on His left;
22.20: and Jehovah says, Who does entice Ahab, and he does go up and fall in Ramoth-Gilead? and this one says thus, and that one is saying thus.
22.21: `And the spirit goes out, and stands before Jehovah, and says, I--I do entice him; and Jehovah says to him, By what?
22.22: and he says, I go out, and have been a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets; and He says, You do entice, and also you are able; go out and do so.
22.23: And now, indeed, Jehovah has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these your prophets, and Jehovah has spoken concerning you--evil.'
22.24: And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah draws nigh, and smites Micaiah on the cheek, and says, `Where is this--he has passed over--the Spirit of Jehovah--from me to speak with you?'
22.25: And Micaiah says, `Indeed, you are seeing on that day, when you go in to the innermost chamber to be hidden.'
22.26: And the king of Israel says, `Take Micaiah, and turn him back to Amon head of the city, and to Joash son of the king,
22.27: and you have said, Thus said the king, Place you this one in the house of restraint, and cause him to eat bread of oppression, and water of oppression, till my coming in peace.'
22.28: And Micaiah says, `If you at all return in peace--Jehovah has not spoken by me;' and he says, `Hear, O peoples, all of them.'
22.29: And the king of Israel goes up, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, to Ramoth-Gilead.
22.30: And the king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat to disguise himself, and to go into battle, `And you, put on your garments.' And the king of Israel disguises himself, and goes into battle.
22.31: And the king of Aram commanded the heads of the charioteers whom he has--thirty and two--saying, `You do not fight with small or with great, but with the king of Israel by himself.'
22.32: And it comes to pass, at the heads of the charioteers seeing Jehoshaphat, that they said, `He is only the king of Israel;' and they turn aside to him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cries out,
22.33: and it comes to pass, at the heads of the charioteers seeing that he is not the king of Israel, that they turn back from after him.
22.34: And a man has drawn with a bow, in his simplicity, and smites the king of Israel between the joinings and the coat of mail, and he says to his charioteer, `Turn your hand, and take me out from the camp, for I have become sick.'
22.35: And the battle increases on that day, and the king has been caused to stand in the chariot, over-against Aram, and he dies in the evening, and the blood of the wound runs out to the midst of the chariot,
22.36: and he causes the cry to pass over through the camp, at the going in of the sun, saying, `Each to his city, and each to his land.'
22.37: And the king dies, and comes into Samaria, and they bury the king in Samaria;
22.38: and one rinses the chariot by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs lick his blood--when the armour they had washed--according to the word of Jehovah that He spoke.
22.39: And the rest of the matters of Ahab, and all that he did, and the house of ivory that he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
22.40: And Ahab lies with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his stead.
22.41: And Jehoshaphat son of Asa has reigned over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel,
22.42: Jehoshaphat is a son of thirty and five years in his reigning, and twenty and five years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
22.43: And he walks in all the way of Asa his father, he has not turned aside from it, to do that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah; only the high places have not turned aside, yet are the people sacrificing and making perfume in high places.
22.44: And Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel;
22.45: and the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he got, and with which he fought, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
22.46: And the remnant of the whoremongers who were left in the days of Asa his father he took away out of the land;
22.47: and there is no king in Edom; he set up a king.
22.48: Jehoshaphat made ships at Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, and they went not, for the ships were broken in Ezion-Geber.
22.49: Then said Ahaziah son of Ahab to Jehoshaphat, `Let my servants go with your servants in the ships;' and Jehoshaphat was not willing.
22.50: And Jehoshaphat lies with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and Jehoram his son reigns in his stead.
22.51: Ahaziah son of Ahab has reigned over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigns over Israel two years,
22.52: and does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and walks in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat who caused Israel to sin,
22.53: and serves the Baal, and bows himself to it, and provokes Jehovah, God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.
